# Claude Code for Empirical Research: A Hands-On Session

This is a three-hour, laptops-open session for PhD students in accounting, finance and economics. You will use Claude Code, an AI agent that runs in your terminal, to take a public SEC dataset to a figure you have checked yourself, turn that work into a reusable skill, and run the checks that make agent-assisted work safe to put in a paper. Most examples are from accounting. You need no prior experience with Claude Code, and Stata users are as welcome as Python users.

::: {.hero-facts}
3 hours · 2 labs · free SEC data only · about 2 hours of prep
:::

## The three hours

::: {.agenda}
| Time | Block | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| 0:00–0:20 | Framing | What an agent can do that a chat window can't, and how you stay in control of it. |
| 0:20–0:45 | Live demo 1 | From an idea on FSDS data to a verified figure, including one planned failure and how the agent recovers. |
| 0:45–1:35 | [Lab 1](lab1.qmd) | You build the same loop on the quarters you downloaded, at one of three tiers, and check it. |
| 1:35–1:45 | Break | |
| 1:45–2:15 | Demo 2 + [Lab 2a](lab2.qmd#lab-2a) | A short EDGAR text demo, then you turn your Lab 1 pipeline into a skill and test it. |
| 2:15–2:40 | [Lab 2b](lab2.qmd#lab-2b) | Three drills on your own repo: a credential audit, a clean-room referee and a deny rule. |
| 2:40–3:00 | Discussion + exit ticket | What this changes for research, using the [readings](readings.qmd) and what you just did. |
:::

The [Session page](session.qmd) has the full agenda with links to the slides and labs.

## What you leave with

By the end of the session you will have four things of your own:

- a pipeline you ran and checked yourself, from a free SEC dataset to a figure with a paper trail (`DATA_PROFILE.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, `LOG.md`) and one number checked against a 10-K on EDGAR;
- a `SKILL.md` built from that pipeline, tested in a fresh session on a request that doesn't name it;
- a credential audit and a clean-room review, both run on your own repository;
- a written answer to what this changes for your own research, on the exit ticket.

Everything in the session uses free SEC data: the Financial Statement Data Sets (FSDS) and EDGAR filings. We do not use WRDS in class. If you want to connect Claude Code to WRDS afterward, the [After Class](after-class.qmd) page links to the full course's WRDS setup.

The session is drawn from a longer six-module course, [Claude Code for Accounting Research](https://johnmbarrios.com/claude-code-accounting/). Taught by [John Barrios](about.qmd), Yale School of Management.
